decisions.reason: The existing same-message Event updates enable_gpio to GPIO5 but leaves led_standby_power_policy incorrectly referring to GPIO3.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Sorry, GPIO3 was from my original ESP32 design — mistake on my side. For 5V_EN you can use GPIO5. Also I realized GPIO22, 23, 25, 27 are not exposed on the WROOM-1 module, so I need to reassign SCL0 (GPIO22→38), SPI MOSI (GPIO23→26). I'll update the docs and send you the full updated GPIO table.

value_updates.led_standby_power_policy: Switch off the entire 5V rail through 5V_EN controlled by GPIO5 when the LEDs are not needed, reducing their standby current to zero

decisions.reason: Changing the GPIO controlling 5V_EN does not alter the daughterboard's LED count, form, selected part, or stated supply voltage.
The interboard interface carries the unchanged 5V_EN signal on pin 7; its connector assignment does not encode the ESP32 GPIO driving that signal.
The GPIO reassignment for the separate 5V boost-enable signal does not change DCDC1 voltage, capacity, or its 3.3V load coverage.
The standalone USB 3.3V supply and source-selection behavior are independent of the 5V_EN GPIO reassignment.
The source decision does not change USB data routing, enumeration, or standalone flashing behavior.
The charge-status interface uses GPIO13 and its separate LED circuitry; changing 5V_EN from GPIO3 to GPIO5 does not alter this state.
The AXP2101 battery and system power-path behavior remains unchanged by reassignment of the separate boost-rail enable GPIO.
The candidate already has a same-message Event that records 5V_EN on GPIO5 together with the SCL0 and SPI MOSI reassignments, so no correction is needed.
The GPIO changes do not affect the selected USB-C connector or its sourceability and substitution requirements.
The candidate already records WROOM-1 from the same message, and the GPIO reassignments do not change the selected module variant.
The battery connector family, pin functions, part, and unresolved pin-order issue are unrelated to the 5V_EN GPIO reassignment.
